rubric.why: Identifies the decline in the species’ population.
rubric.description: States that the species has a declining or greatly reduced population.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying the decline in population.

rubric.why: States the defining danger faced by the species.
rubric.description: States that the species is at risk of extinction.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that the species may become extinct.

modelAnswer: An endangered species is a species whose population has declined so much that it is at risk of extinction.

rubric.why: Describes the characteristic small, bubble-like shape of a bleb.
rubric.description: Describes a bleb as a small, bubble-like bulge or protrusion.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying its shape as a small bulge or protrusion.

rubric.description: States that the bulge is on the plasma membrane or cell surface.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying the membrane or cell surface as its location.

modelAnswer: Blebs are small, bubble-like bulges or protrusions of the plasma membrane on the cell surface.

items.followUp: How does an enzyme affect the activation energy of a reaction?

rubric.why: Identifies the complex formed when an enzyme binds its substrate.
rubric.description: States that an enzyme binds to its substrate to form an enzyme-substrate complex.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for naming or describing formation of the enzyme-substrate complex.

rubric.why: States the benefit of the complex in enzyme action.
rubric.description: States that the complex lowers activation energy and thereby helps the reaction proceed faster.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that activation energy is lowered or that the reaction proceeds faster.

modelAnswer: An enzyme binds to its substrate to form an enzyme-substrate complex.
This complex lowers the activation energy, so the reaction proceeds faster.

rubric.why: Explains that activation energy supplies the initial energy needed to start a reaction.
rubric.description: States that activation energy is needed to initiate a chemical reaction.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for explaining its role in starting the reaction.

rubric.why: Explains why reactants need an initial energy input.
rubric.description: States that this energy helps weaken or break bonds in the reactants.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for linking activation energy to weakening or breaking bonds.

modelAnswer: Activation energy is necessary to provide the initial energy that starts a chemical reaction.
It helps weaken or break bonds in the reactants so they can undergo the reaction.
